## Automated AI review

> **Community review:** Independent automated community review, unaffiliated with the Omarchy team, intended to help prepare PRs for their review.

**Verified:** at `ce9471c3`, both findings from the [earlier review](https://github.com/omacom/omarchy/pull/12982#issuecomment-5808140482) and its optional palette note are resolved, as described in the [author's reply](https://github.com/omacom/omarchy/pull/12982#issuecomment-5818604711). No new issue was found in the changed code.

| Earlier item | Status at `ce9471c3` |
|---|---|
| Cloud and fog strips regenerated on every popup open | Resolved |
| Default location setup never uses the Open-Meteo code or day flag | Resolved |
| Optional: sky colours follow global rather than popup colours | Resolved |

### Strip caching

**Verified:** strip geometry now lives in `layerCache` on the sky item, outside the Canvas. The cache is keyed by columns, rows, noise period, kind, noise scales, top-only, density and seed, and colours, opacity and scroll speed are applied at paint time. In Quickshell v0.3.1 the layer-shell window is still deleted on hide, but the QML content item survives. Qt 6.11.2 still frees the Canvas image, so a reopen now replays cached runs instead of recomputing noise:

```text
popup opens (same geometry)
  before: Canvas.onPaint -> full noise field recomputed (65k to 170k noise samples per scene)
  after:  Canvas.onPaint -> layerRuns() cache hit -> fillRect replay, 0 noise samples
```

A comparison of the strip functions from both revisions, extracted and run in a JavaScript engine (not QML), covered 960 cases: scenes, intensities, wind, day/night, dark/light palettes and three sizes. Every case produced identical drawing commands, including cached geometry repainted in new colours. Fog alpha levels are unchanged. The storm band and the lightning-flash band share one geometry. Both fog strips fit within the two-entry cache. Intensity and size changes rebuild the geometry. Night, wind and palette changes do not.

New geometry is still generated synchronously on first open and when geometry inputs change, as the reply states.

### Sky data source

**Verified:** the sky resolves from `openMeteoCurrent || current`. Auto-detected and name-only locations therefore use the WMO code, day flag, intensity and hail once the Open-Meteo response has arrived. The glyph fallback remains when that response is missing. The new panel-binding test evaluates the panel's actual binding text. It passes at this head and fails against the previous revision with the earlier symptom: code 96 at night resolved to storm, moderate intensity, no hail, day palette.

### Popup palette

**Verified:** the sky's light-surface check, ink and blends now use `Color.popups.background` and `Color.popups.text`, the colours the card is painted with. The static layer repaints on any palette change. The strips pick up new colours without rebuilding geometry.

---

## Review information

**Test scope:** Source review of head `ce9471c3` against the earlier reviewed head `7cf2f9dc`, together with Quickshell v0.3.1 and Qt 6.11.2 source. The JavaScript portion of `test/shell.d/weather-test.sh` passed at the head (95 checks, with Deno standing in for Node) in an isolated sandbox. The new binding and strip-cache checks failed as expected when run against the earlier revision. The strip comparison ran the extracted functions outside QML. The author's live reopen timings were not independently repeated. On-screen appearance and translucent popup backgrounds were not checked.

**AI process:** Opus 5.5 Medium coordination and synthesis, independent Opus 5.5 Xhigh and GPT 6 Sol Xhigh technical assessments of this follow-up with a targeted cross-check, Opus 5.5 Medium editorial check.
